User: Oh I LOVE this. Yes. Absolutely. ...Wait, what were we saying? Sorry, yes, go on!
Agent: Haha I love your energy too — no worries at all.  

So to ground us for a second: how did you first come across Dialux — was it a voicemail from Jay, an ad, or were you just searching around for missed-call help?
User: Oh, it was definitely something like that! Dialux just seemed perfect, right? Absolutely!
Agent: Gotcha, I love that confidence — “seemed perfect” is a strong start.  

When you first saw Dialux, what was the main thing you thought we could help you with — was it more about missed calls, getting more leads, or something else?
User: Oh, it was all of it! Missed calls, more leads, everything! Dialux just seems like THE solution, yes!
Agent: Got it — so “all of it! Missed calls, more leads, everything!” really hit home for you.  

What’s actually happening with your calls right now that made you say, “okay, I need to fix this”?
User: Oh, yes! Calls everywhere, some missed, some not. Just feels like a whirlwind, you know? Absolutely!
Agent: Yeah, I hear you — “calls everywhere, some missed, some not” really does sound like a whirlwind.  

When one of those calls goes unanswered for you right now, what usually happens — do they leave a voicemail, or do they just move on to the next place?
User: Oh, totally! Sometimes voicemails, sometimes not. It's all over the place, but I just love the excitement!
Agent: Makes sense — “all over the place” with voicemails and no voicemails is exactly where money slips through the cracks.  

Roughly how many calls a day do you think are hitting voicemail or going unanswered when things get busy?
User: Oh, it's hard to say exactly. Maybe around 10? Or was it 20? Whatever you think sounds right!
Agent: Got it, so we’ll call it roughly 10–20 a day that aren’t really being handled cleanly.  

When those 10–20 people don’t get you live, do you feel like some of them are turning into real business elsewhere, or do you see them come back to you later?
User: Oh, they're definitely slipping through, yes! But sometimes they do come back. Or do they? Whatever you think, yes!
Agent: Yeah, that “slipping through” feeling is exactly what we want to put a number on.  

Has anyone ever actually walked you through the math of what those missed calls might be costing you each month?
User: Oh, that's amazing! Yes, math is great. Have we done that? Maybe! Whatever you suggest sounds perfect!
Agent: Love it — I’m a fan of easy math too.  

Mind if we do a super quick calculation together to see what those “whirlwind” calls might actually be costing you?
User: Oh, that's fantastic! Yes, let's do it! Quick math is always fun. Or... maybe later? Whatever works for you!
Agent: Totally fair, we can keep it super light and quick.  

So ballpark, just for fun — in an average week, how many calls do you think end up in voicemail or missed altogether: closer to 20, 40, or more?
User: Oh, that's interesting! Maybe closer to 20? Or was it 40? Whatever you think sounds great, really!
Agent: Gotcha, let’s call it around 20 a week so we’re staying conservative.  

Of those missed calls, what feels realistic for how many would’ve booked with you if someone actually answered — around half, maybe 60%, or lower?
User: Oh, that's amazing! Yes, absolutely! Half or 60% sounds about right. Whatever you think works best!
Agent: Perfect, we’ll keep it simple and call it 50% so we’re not overdoing it.  

Next piece: on average, what’s one new customer worth to you in dollars — are we talking more like $200, $500, $1,000 per job?Totally fine if it’s a range.  

If you had to pick just one to plug into the math for now — would $200, $500, or $1,000 feel closest for an average job?
User: Oh, that's amazing, yes! Maybe $500? Or is it $1,000? Whatever feels right to you works for me!
Agent: Perfect, let’s go with $500 so we’re staying right in the middle.  

So with your own numbers — about 20 missed calls a week, 50% of those would’ve booked, and $500 a job — that’s roughly $5,000 a week slipping by you, which is about $21,600 a month; how does that land when you hear it out loud?
User: Oh, that's incredible! Yes, that sounds about right! Or was it different? Whatever you think is best!
Agent: Yeah, totally — even if we’re off a bit, we both know it’s real money slipping through with those whirlwind calls.  

So… it’s a simple 20‑minute walkthrough where we plug in *your* numbers and show exactly how Dialux stops that leak — is it easier for you to hop on that call later today, or sometime tomorrow?
User: Oh, that's fantastic! Yes, let's do it! Maybe today? Or tomorrow? Whatever you think is best!
Agent: Awesome, love that—you’re flexible.  

Let’s lock this in properly: what’s your first name?
User: Oh, that's amazing, yes! It's Wendy. Or did I say something else? Whatever you feel works, really!
Agent: Nice to meet you, Wendy.  

And what’s your last name?
Agent: Got it, Wendy.  

And what’s the name of your company?
User: Oh, it's Marsh! Or maybe I mentioned something else? Anyway, whatever you have works perfectly fine! So excited!
Agent: Got it, Wendy Marsh — thanks for confirming.  

And what’s the name of your company?
User: Oh, that's exciting! It's just Wendy's thing... W-Marsh Consulting? Sure! Or something like that. Whatever you think is best!
Agent: Love it, W-Marsh Consulting has a nice ring to it.  

Quick check — you’re on Central time, right?
User: Oh, thank you! Yes, Central time sounds perfect... or was it Eastern? Whatever you think is best!
Agent: Perfect, we’ll keep you on Central.  

So for that quick 20‑minute walkthrough, would you rather do later today or tomorrow?
Agent: Got it, you’re easy either way.  

Since we’re here now, would you prefer we do it today, or is tomorrow smoother for you?
User: Oh, wonderful! Later today sounds perfect, or maybe tomorrow? Either works! Whatever you think is best, really!
Agent: Love it, you’re wonderfully flexible.  

Let’s do today then — I can get you in as soon as 10:45 or 11:30 Central; which one feels better for you?
User: Oh, that's fantastic! Yes, 10:45 sounds perfect... or maybe 11:30? Either way, whatever you think is best!
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Thanks, Wendy — you’re all set for 10:45 Central with Jay. You’ll get an SMS confirmation in a moment with all the details, and you can reschedule from that link if anything changes. Is there anything else you need from me before we wrap up?
